The booklet is 19 pages: idx 0 is the bilingual cover, idx 1 the Hindi General Instructions, and every ODD index 1..17 is the Hindi page for the English page that FOLLOWS it (Hindi first, then English); idx 18 is the last page and is English. ALL 19 PAGES ACCOUNTED FOR, and the parity was MEASURED rather than assumed: a per-page Devanagari/Latin census gives Devanagari EXACTLY 0 on all nine even pages, and 448-2008 Devanagari characters on all nine odd pages whose Latin content (29-76 chars) is entirely chemical formulae inside the Hindi text plus the page furniture. So NO odd page carries English overflow, there is no mid-paper parity inversion and there is no blank trailing page. English content does spill from one EVEN page to the NEXT EVEN page (Q18 -> idx10, Q30 -> idx16, Q32 -> idx18), which is harmless. Question numbers extracted per English page run 1-2 / 3-7 / 8-12 / 13-18 / 19-23 / 24-28 / 29-30 / 31-32 / 33 — an unbroken 1..33. STRUCTURE agrees with the printed General Instructions exactly (33 questions, five sections, A 1-16 @1, B 17-21 @2, C 22-28 @3, D 29-30 case-based @4, E 31-33 @5) and the ASSERTION-REASON BAND IS PRINTED AS 13 to 16 (read off idx 8, full size), i.e. the standard full70 position. DECIMAL POINTS ARE RAISED on this paper — U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT, confirmed both at 3x zoom and in the PDF text layer (2·0, 1·87, 0·347, 0·01, 0·76, 1·5, 1·86, 3·905, 40·9, 349·6) -> written as 0{\cdot}347. NOTE the marking scheme prints ORDINARY dots throughout (1.86, 0.693, 1.5); the PAPER wins, per the addendum. INTERNAL CHOICE: instruction (viii) prints NO COUNTS, so the roster was established TWO independent ways that agree exactly — (a) bare 'OR' lines in the paper's own text layer, which appear on idx 8, 12, 14, 16 (x3) and 18 with a matching Hindi 'अथवा' on idx 7, 11, 13, 15 (x3) and 17, and (b) a question-by-question walk of the marking scheme, which reprints both branches. SEVEN alternatives: Q18, Q26, Q31, Q32, Q33 (whole-question) plus Q29(c) and Q30(b) (sub-part level inside a case study). Two scheme 'OR's were correctly EXCLUDED as equivalent-forms-of-the-answer rather than choices — Q25 ('Tf = -1.55 C OR Tf = 273.15 - 1.55 = 271.6 K') and Q28 ('t = 0.598 x 10^10 years OR 6 x 10^9 years'); neither question prints an OR on the paper. ANSWERS: all 16 Section-A letters taken VERBATIM from the marking scheme's Section-A table (ms idx 2) and uppercased; none derived. Confirmed a second, independent way by extracting that table from the scheme's text layer — C D D B A C B A C D A A A C D D, identical to the vision read. THERE ARE NO KEYED MCQs OUTSIDE SECTION A (Section-D case studies are wholly subjective), which is the expected full70/Chemistry shape. VOIDS: NONE. All 8 marking-scheme pages were read by vision AND swept by a purpose-built scanner (_tmp/_tmp_2026-56-3-2_voidscan.py) validated against all 16 printed examples in SCIENCE_ADDENDUM.md plus 8 negative cases from this very scheme, scanning PAGE-JOINED text so a note split across two lines still matches; that scanner found ZERO unconditional awards, ZERO keyless voids, ZERO dual keys and ZERO medium-scoped notes. Its only two hits are CONDITIONAL boilerplate attached to worked ANSWERS, not to questions ('or any other correct example' on Q26(b), 'or any other suitable reagent' on Q29(a)), so they get no field. Worth knowing for later papers: contrary to the addendum's general claim that 2026 schemes are page images, THIS scheme has a usable 12,244-character text layer. RELATIONSHIP TO THE OPENER 56/3/1: the two sets draw on one pool but are HEAVILY RE-AUTHORED and RENUMBERED — see the per-row _flag fields. 28 of the 44 rows are content-identical to an opener row and carry its stem/options byte-for-byte after being confirmed against MY page; 16 are genuinely different questions. 25 of the 28 reuse the opener text deliberately; Q1, Q2 and Q6 were transcribed INDEPENDENTLY and came out byte-identical anyway, which is the convergence the brief predicts. TYPOGRAPHY CONFORMANCE, stated openly: on four shared strings the printed glyph is U+2212 MINUS SIGN and the opener transcribed U+2013 EN DASH — verified in BOTH papers' text layers, so the opener is uniformly the less faithful reading and this is not a per-paper difference. Rows NOT shared with the opener are transcribed faithfully: Q21's '- OH' and Q22(c)'s 'CH3 - I' really are U+2013 EN DASH on this paper, which therefore uses both characters. questions.context: Alcohols have higher boiling points than other compounds, namely hydrocarbons, ethers and haloalkanes of comparable molecular masses. On oxidation, primary alcohols yield aldehydes with mild oxidizing agents and carboxylic acids with strong oxidizing agents. Secondary alcohols yield ketones on oxidation while tertiary alcohols are resistant to oxidation. Ethers may be prepared by dehydration of alcohols and Williamson synthesis. The C – O bond in ethers can be cleaved by hydrogen halides. The presence of – OH group in phenols activates the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution and directs the incoming group to ortho and para positions due to resonance effect. In presence of NaOH, phenol generates phenoxide ion which is even more reactive than phenol. Thus, in alkaline medium, phenol undergoes Kolbe’s reaction.

questions.context: Living systems are made up of various complex biomolecules like carbohydrates, proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, etc. Proteins and carbohydrates are essential constituents of our food. In addition, some simple molecules like vitamins and mineral salts also play an important role in the functions of organisms. All proteins are polymers of \(\alpha\)-amino acids. Proteins can be classified into two types on the basis of their molecular shape — Fibrous and Globular proteins. Vitamins are accessory food factors required in the diet. Nucleic acids are the polymers of nucleotides which in turn consist of a base, a pentose sugar and phosphate moiety. There are two types of nucleic acids — DNA and RNA. Nucleic acids are responsible for the transfer of characters from parents to offsprings.

Given : \(\mathrm{E^{o}_{Zn^{2+}/Zn}} = -\,0{\cdot}76\ \mathrm{V}\)
[\(\log 10 = 1\)]
(ii) Write anode, cathode and overall reaction involved in dry cell.
(iii) Equilibrium constant (\(\mathrm{K_c}\)) is related to \(\mathrm{E^{o}_{cell}}\), but not to \(\mathrm{E_{cell}}\). Why ?

(i) The conductivity of \(0{\cdot}001\) M solution of acetic acid is \(3{\cdot}905 \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{S\ cm^{-1}}\). Calculate its molar conductivity and degree of dissociation (\(\alpha\)).
Given : \(\lambda^{o}_{\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}} = 40{\cdot}9\ \mathrm{S\ cm^2\ mol^{-1}}\)
\(\lambda^{o}_{\mathrm{H^+}} = 349{\cdot}6\ \mathrm{S\ cm^2\ mol^{-1}}\)
(ii) Give reasons for the following :
(I) Why does a mercury cell deliver a constant voltage for its entire life ?
(II) Why is it necessary to use salt bridge in a galvanic cell ?

questions.subtopic: General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)
questions.stem:
(i) Describe giving reason which one of the following pairs has the property indicated :
(I) Fe or Cu – higher melting point
(II) \(\mathrm{Ti^{3+}}\) or \(\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}\) – coloured in aqueous solution
(III) Cr or Zn – higher third ionisation enthalpy
(ii) Write the ionic equations for the oxidizing action of \(\mathrm{MnO_4^-}\) in acidic medium with :
(I) \(\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\) ion
(II) \(\mathrm{I^-}\) ion
questions._flag: Sub-part (ii) is about the oxidising action of permanganate, which sits under 'Some Important Compounds of Transition Elements'. Filed on 'General Properties of the Transition Elements (d-Block)', which covers sub-part (i) — the larger half, 3 of the 5 marks. Separately, TYPOGRAPHY CONFORMED: the three dashes in sub-part (i) are printed as U+2212 MINUS SIGN on this paper AND on the opener (verified in both text layers), but the opener transcribed U+2013 EN DASH; the opener's character is kept so this identical question dedups.

questions.subtopic: Some Important Compounds of Transition Elements
questions.stem:
(i) A black-brown coloured solid (A) when fused with KOH in the presence of air, produces a dark green coloured compound (B) which on electrolytic oxidation in alkaline medium gives a dark purple coloured compound (C). Identify (A), (B) and (C). Write the reactions involved.
(ii) What happens when an acidic solution of the green compound (B) is allowed to stand for some time ? Also write the equation involved. What is this type of reaction called ?

questions.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
questions.stem:
(i) Write the product(s) when :
(I) One mol of ethanal is treated with 1 mol of \(\mathrm{CH_3OH}\) in the presence of dry HCl gas.
(II) Benzaldehyde is treated with conc. NaOH.
(III) Ethanoic acid is heated in the presence of \(\mathrm{P_2O_5}\).
(ii) Write a simple chemical test to distinguish between Ethanal and Propanal.
(iii) Write the name of the reagent to transform Allyl alcohol to Propenal.

questions.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Aldehydes and Ketones
questions.stem:
(i) Draw the structure of the semicarbazone of acetone.
(ii) Why are \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms of aldehydes and ketones acidic in nature ?
(iii) Arrange the following compounds in increasing order of their reactivity towards HCN :
\(\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}\), \(\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\), \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-CO-CH_3}\)
(iv) Write the reaction involved in Etard reaction.
(v) Write the product when cyclohexanecarbaldehyde reacts with Zn(Hg)/conc. HCl.
questions._figure: ILLUSTRATIVE — sub-part (v)'s reactant is DRAWN on THIS paper's own page and was read here rather than copied: a PLAIN hexagon with NO inner circle and NO double bonds, i.e. a cyclohexane ring, bearing —CHO, confirmed at 6x zoom. Named losslessly in the stem as cyclohexanecarbaldehyde, so the row is answerable from text; the reading is corroborated by THIS paper's own marking scheme (ms idx 7), whose answer to (v) is a plain hexagon bearing CH3, i.e. methylcyclohexane, the Clemmensen product. Sub-part (iii)'s third compound is also drawn, as '(CH3)3C − C − CH3' with the carbonyl O below the chain, and is transcribed as the typeable condensed structure \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-CO-CH_3}\). Page idx 18.
